## College Laptop Comparison Snapshot

You have **4 options** and **4 hard constraints**:
- Budget: under **$1,200**
- Battery: at least **8 hours**
- Weight: under **1.6 kg**
- RAM: at least **16 GB**

## Laptop Fit Comparison

| Option | Price | RAM | SSD | Weight | Battery | Passes Constraints? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A | $999 | 16 GB | 512 GB | 1.4 kg | 10 h | **Yes** |
| B | $1,149 | 16 GB | 1 TB | 1.8 kg | 9 h | **No** |
| C | $899 | 8 GB | 512 GB | 1.3 kg | 12 h | **No** |
| D | $1,199 | 32 GB | 1 TB | 1.5 kg | 7 h | **No** |

## Best Choice for College Use

**Recommended option: A**
- Meets **all 4 constraints**
- Strong balance of **price, portability, and battery**
- Best fit for a typical college laptop where reliability matters more than extra storage or RAM

### Why the others miss
- **B**: too heavy at **1.8 kg**
- **C**: only **8 GB RAM**, below the minimum
- **D**: battery is only **7 hours**, below the minimum

## Best Chart Setup for Your Presentation

### Best overall: **Bar chart**
Use a **bar chart** with one cluster per laptop and four bars per cluster:
- **Price**
- **RAM**
- **Weight**
- **Battery**

Why this works:
- Easy to compare each model side by side
- Makes it obvious which models fail a constraint
- Good for a general audience

### Best for trade-off analysis: **Radar chart**
Use a **radar chart** if you want to show the balance between:
- Lower price
- Higher RAM
- Lower weight
- Higher battery

Why this works:
- Best for showing “shape” of the laptop profile
- Good for highlighting that **A** is the most balanced overall
- Less precise than a bar chart, but visually stronger for trade-offs

## Quick Recommendation for Visualization

- Use a **bar chart** if your audience needs **clear, factual comparison**
- Use a **radar chart** if your audience needs **trade-off storytelling**
- If you can include only one chart, choose **bar chart + simple pass/fail color coding**

## Presentation Tip

For the cleanest slide:
- Color **A** in green as the only passing option
- Mark **B, C, D** in red or amber
- Add a small note: **“Only A satisfies all requirements.”**

## Sources

- Chart design guidance for comparisons: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/create-a-chart-from-start-to-finish-0baf399e-4f4c-4b0a-8f0b-9f1f6d8f9b0b
- Radar chart use cases: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2018/06/14/when-to-use-a-radar-chart/
